content:
{
  "claim": "recover_json_object treats a JSON object nested inside a top-level array as a top-level candidate, even though the documentation says only top-level balanced objects are candidates.",
  "expected": "For content `[{\"a\": 1}]`, recover_json_object should raise RecordError because there is no top-level object; the only object is nested inside a list.",
  "observed": "It returns the dict `{\"a\": 1}` (with an empty duplicates tuple) because the top-level scanner raw-decodes the `{` inside the list and appends it to top_level.",
  "reproducer": "[{\"a\": 1}]",
  "source_basis": "The docstring states: \"Every top-level balanced object in the text is a candidate\" and \"an object nested inside another is not a candidate of its own.\" The phrase \"top-level balanced object\" excludes objects nested inside any JSON value, including arrays.",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Any text where the only JSON object(s) are nested inside a top-level JSON array; recover_json_object will incorrectly return one of them instead of raising RecordError.",
  "uncertainty": "The docstring explicitly mentions only objects nested inside another object, not arrays; however 'top-level' normally excludes arrays. If the intended meaning of 'top-level' is only not nested inside another object, this may not be a defect."
}
